subject: Acme migration: traffic-shift playbook and enterprise comms (model v1 -> v2)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme migration kickoff — traffic shift & comms asks

Team — looping you in on ACME-449 (Acme Corp). Sales flagged a required move from our legacy endpoint/model (api/v1/generate, model=redwood-infer-v1) to the new v2 family. This customer is on a reserved plan and is a revenue-impacting account for Q3.

High-level asks from Sales/CS:
- Draft a coordinated traffic-shift playbook (can we do a phased percentage shift + feature-flag rollout?).
- Clear comms cadence + templated notice for their infrastructure/ops (they want dates + rollback triggers).
- Exemption criteria: when is a dedicated pool exception justified and process to get it approved?
- SLA/latency impact statement for their contracts and any credit discussion (they asked for an up-front mitigation).
- Timeline: want cutover window in September; they asked for a one-week freeze around quarter-end (Sept 30).

I attached a preliminary impact spreadsheet and a draft customer notice. Please reply with owners (tech lead, comms lead, legal touchpoint), a realistic timeline (eta for a safe phased shift), and any hard blocker. I want a one-page MAP to share with Acme tomorrow.

Attachments: acme-map-v2-impact.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), migration-draft-notice.docx (draft notice)

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
(attachment: acme-map-v2-impact.xlsx) (attachment: migration-draft-notice.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme migration kickoff — traffic shift & comms asks

Thanks Ben — I can own the product-side playbook. Quick notes after scanning the impact file:
- Feasibility: We can support a phased traffic-shift using route-by-header + model-variant feature flags. I recommend a 0/10/25/50/100 staged ramp over 4 weeks with monitoring gates at each step.
- Risk: For sequences >2048 tokens we may see up to ~2% higher p95 on v2 for a subset of prompts; we should identify those templates and offer an exemption path.
- Shim approach: We can provide a routing shim (api/v1 -> compatible v2 variant) for 60 days. If Acme needs longer, ops can extend to 90 days but requires a dedicated pool request.
- Docs: I will update the API migration guide and add a migration checklist.

Action items I propose:
1) Marissa — produce a 1-page migration playbook + tech checklist by EOD 8/17.
2) Aditya — take point on customer-facing comms and the templated notice; please coordinate with Laura for CS tone.
3) Prioym — confirm capacity windows and any perf caveats; need automated rollback hooks if gate fails.

I created a living doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XaZ-migration-playbook (please comment).

-Marissa
Sr PM, Platform
(attachment: MAP_ACME-449.pdf)

From: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme migration kickoff — traffic shift & comms asks

Ben/Marissa — operational constraints and recommended guardrails from Infra:
- Capacity: We have a maintenance window for scheduled configuration changes 02:00-05:00 PT; larger routing changes should happen in that window to minimize impact.
- Shim: We can implement a compatible routing shim for up to 90 days but prefer 60 days as default. The shim will maintain KV/cache semantics but will not backfill new quantization artifacts; that may produce small quality drift for edge prompts.
- Monitoring: We will surface a per-tenant regression dashboard (latency, error-rate, token-cost) and an automated rollback if error-rate increases by >1.5x or p95 latency increases by >20% against baseline.
- Dedicated pool exception: To approve a dedicated GPU pool for a customer migration we need Product sign-off + Finance approval for a three-month minimum commit. Requests should include expected qps and token distribution.

I also flagged a potential perf risk for long-context batched calls (customer-specific prompts that use 6k+ context) — could hit the memory quantization path and degrade throughput. If Acme uses that, we should schedule a pre-cutover load test.

- Prioym
Infra SRE — Serving
(attachment: infra-migration-ops-guidelines.txt)

From: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme migration kickoff — traffic shift & comms asks

Thanks Ben & team — appreciate the early visibility. A few things from our side:
- Quarter-end freeze: We need a freeze window between Sept 27–Oct 3; can you confirm you can avoid disruptive changes then?
- SLA impact: We need a short write-up confirming whether the migration will affect SLA calculations or trigger credits if latency/regressions occur during the ramp. If there are any service credits we need the mechanism defined.
- Pre-cutover load test: Yes — we'll run a session with our platform team. Please propose two candidate dates in the week of Sept 8.
- Can you include a short risk matrix for our execs about rollback scenarios and expected visibility?

We are available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow 8/18 at 11:00 PT — does that work for your team?

— Samantha
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Acme migration — consolidated plan, owners, and next steps

Folks — thanks for the quick responses. Capturing decisions and owners so we can move to a customer MAP:
- Product playbook: Marissa -> deliver 1-page playbook + tech checklist by EOD 8/17 (status: done, see doc).
- Customer comms: Aditya + Laura -> finalize templated notice and send to Acme by 8/20.
- Infra ops & rollback hooks: Prioym -> deliver automated rollback thresholds and availability of shim (ops window confirmed).
- Legal/Finance: Ben -> coordinate any credit/contract language; we should propose a goodwill credit tied to measured regression if we miss p95 thresholds.
- Pre-cutover load test: Suggested windows Sept 8 or Sept 10 (Prioym please confirm).
- Freeze window: We will honor Acme's Sept 27–Oct 3 freeze; no cutover during that week.
- Dedicated pool exception: If Acme requests a dedicated pool, we will require a three-month commit. Product must document expected QPS and token distribution for approval.

Next steps:
1) Aditya/Laura — send templated comms + proposed cutover calendar to Acme by 8/20.
2) Prioym — confirm test dates and provide a short ops runbook by 8/24.
3) Ben — I will propose the MAP and the internal exec note; will include suggested credit mechanics.

I scheduled the kickoff sync with Acme for 8/18 11:00 PT (calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-migration-kickoff). Please join.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_ACME-449.pdf)
